title: Black Clover Season 2 Preview Reveals First Look at Big Transformations
content:
Black Clover has finally made its return to screens with its highly anticipated second season, and the anime is showing off the first look at some big transformations with the preview for its next episode. Black Clover Season 2 is now airing its episodes as part of the Fall 2026 anime schedule, and with it fans have been thrown right back into the conflict. Asta and the others have been readying for a raid on the Spade Kingdom, and it’s time for these rematches to kick off in full.

Black Clover Season 2’s premiere saw the Magic Knights making their way into the Spade Kingdom to face off against the members of the Dark Triad , and now it’s time for those fights to actually kick in as the Magic Knights reveal the fruits of their few days of training for this exact moment. And the first look at Black Clover Season 2 Episode 2 actually shows these new power ups off for the first time. Check out the images in the gallery below.

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 2 Confirms Release Date & Synopsis

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 2 is titled “The Gate to Hell” and will be making its debut in Japan on October 10th, and will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll when it hits for fans in North America and other international territories. The synopsis for the episode teases the showdowns that had been seen in the first episode too as “Charlotte confronts Vanica, who harbors the demon Megicula, the source of the curse, while Yuno faces Zenon, who kidnapped Vangeance right before his eyes.”

As for the other conflicts, Black Clover teases that the episode will then see, “Jack and Nacht, though struggling, are fighting on equal footing with Dante, who wields the strongest physical magic.” But as teased by one of the preview images, it won’t just be the Dark Triad that needs to be dealt with as a mysterious pair of new Devils will be making their debut in the episode too. Which means that the series will be gearing up for an even bigger crisis long before Asta even makes his way to the scene.

What’s Next for Black Clover Season 2?

Black Clover Season 2 won’t be around for nearly as long as the first season did, and that’s even more evident after the premiere episode . The Spade Kingdom Raid arc chapters from Yuki Tabata’s original manga really aren’t that long, and when accounting for the chapters that are pretty much all fight scenes, it seems like the new season is going to be adapting the chapters at a steady clip. The premiere takes on a little under five chapters, and this preview teases the second episode is going to do the same.

The twins showing up here teases about another four or so chapters covered within this second episode, and that pace further teases that Black Clover Season 2 might only be lasting for a single cour of episodes for the Fall. The anime has yet to confirm its episode order for its return, so it’s something to keep an eye out for as the series continues to work towards Asta’s big fights to come . What are you hoping to see in Black Clover ‘s next Season 2 episode? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Naruto’s Live-Action Movie Has Way Bigger Plans Than You Think
content:
A new report is teasing that if the new Naruto live-action movie ends up being a success, there could be way more movies planned than any fan could have ever expected. Masashi Kishimoto’s Naruto recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and with it has made a return with all kinds of new projects. Not only are fans going to be treated to a full revival of the classic anime series , but there’s also a live-action feature film adaptation that’s set to go into full production in the near future.

Naruto has kicked off a global casting search for its new live-action feature film debut , and new details about the project have been steadily making their way online through multiple reports. It’s yet to be revealed if any of these reports will pan out, but one of the most curious comes from notable leaker Daniel RPK as the report notes that there could end up being “7-8 films overall” by the time the live-action Naruto franchise wraps up if everything goes well.

Naruto Could Get 8 Live-Action Movies Like Harry Potter

As fans know too well (and have criticized the anime about for decades), Naruto is a very long series. It comes from the earlier eras of Shueisha’s Shonen Jump magazine where creators were encouraged to keep their stories going for a long time, and Naruto spans multiple eras, arcs, and even has two major halves to its story following a time skip. Adapting such a massive story would be an ordeal , which is why the report notes that the plan for the franchise is to follow the Harry Potter model and working it out over seven or eight films.

“Part 1” of the original series would be a trilogy of films, and then the events of Naruto: Shippuden would then wrap up the second half with three or four films. The early story reports for this debut film teases an adaptation of the Land of Waves arc, which would be a suitable start to the entire film franchise . But if there’s a success, then it does raise a lot of questions about not only how long it would take to adapt the story but whether or not something of that nature is even possible.

Will Naruto’s Live-Action Movie Even Work?

This report does feel a bit like it’s putting the cart before the horse for now as the first film hasn’t even started production. This eight film projection is clearly just an early plan for the best possible outcome, but that’s not exactly feasible within the current Hollywood feature film market. Director Destin Daniel Cretton is taking on the film, but is in such high demand that he’s likely going to return to the Spider-Man franchise (or some other notable project ) after Naruto wraps up its production. It’d make an even longer wait for a sequel, let along eight different films.

That’s also not factoring in any potential changes to Naruto ‘s original story. Reports of potential character alterations are already making fans upset, and this is all before any big changes to its story are made. There could be eight different films, but it would be even more realistic to shoot for a trilogy that has a complete story and ending. This live-action version is going to be different than fans will expect, so don’t really hold out hope for a long film franchise either. It’s going to be altered to make it more streamlined for this new version of the story.

How many live-action Naruto films would you want to see? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

HT – Daniel RPK

title: 30 Years Ago, Yu-Gi-Oh Changed the World With a Whole New Kind of Game
content:
Collectible trading card games have been huge within tabletop spaces for decades, with Magic: The Gathering setting the stage for other massive properties to rise in popularity. Interestingly, Magic: The Gathering became such a global phenomenon that it had begun to inspire works in mediums separated entirely from tabletop games, including manga. Kazuki Takahashi, the mangaka behind Yu-Gi-Oh! , was one such creator inspired by the TCG giant, and released an anthology series blending elements of the horror genre with popular games. One of the chapters, aptly titled Magic & Wizards , became so popular with readers that it spiraled into its own original series that has since taken over the world.

In the fall on 1996, Kazuki Takahashi released Yu-Gi-Oh! , a long-form project inspired by his Magic & Wizards oneshot . The original series was picked up and subsequently serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump , and ran for just over seven years before coming to an end. Yu-Gi-Oh! quickly became a global phenomenon, selling over 40 million copies as of writing and spinning into a massively popular trading card game of the same name, with its popularity being on par with Pokemon and the franchise that inspired it, Magic: The Gathering .

Yu-Gi-Oh! Created The Perfect Recipe For Global Success

In the late 1990s, tabletop games focused on collectible trading cards were new, but rapidly picking up in popularity. One of the biggest appeals to mediums like anime and manga playing with components of games is their ability to harness the joys of escapism into a new form of fantasy, and Yu-Gi-Oh! captures that concept perfectly. The series follows an awkward teenager named Yugi Mutou, who, despite being timid and struggling to make friends at school, loves playing games.

After acquiring and solving the Millennium Puzzle, Yugi is hopeful that the ancient artifact will grant his wish of being able to make friends, but in the process, his body becomes the host for a mysterious spirit with an almost malicious love for gaming. As Yugi gets drawn deeper into the world of “Duel Monsters” — the in-universe card game played in the series, the more familiar he grows with the spirit as it begins taking control of his body to challenge other duelists to dangerous Shadow Games.

Yu-Gi-Oh! introduces high stakes for its duelists , and an eccentric supporting cast of allies and enemies that Yugi encounters over the course of the series, which made it an instant hit with readers. The series was quickly picked up for an anime adaptation, releasing only two years after the manga began serializing in Weekly Shonen Jump . Furthermore, the fictional Duel Monsters game was later turned into a very real trading card game sharing the same name as the manga in 1999, and became a massive commercial hit with tabletop gaming fans around the globe.

Yu-Gi-Oh! Continues To Be A Multimedia Titan

Yu-Gi-Oh! ‘s trading card game adaptation became far more than additional promo to help sell copies of the manga to readers. In fact, the game caught on like wildfire following its release, with the North American launch of the trading card game in 2002 raking in over $17 million in just its first few months on store shelves. By 2009, the card game had sold over 22 billion individual cards around the globe, with that number rapidly skyrocketing every year that followed. Many first edition cards from this era of Yu-Gi-Oh! have become highly sought after collectibles as well, with original printings for cards like Blue-Eyes White Dragon selling for as high as $30,000 to $45,000.

The franchise’s popularity is still going strong, with Master Duel making the game more accessible than ever before for fans of the TCG, and new anime projects in the works from Konami with the upcoming releasing of The Chronicles , which will be a monthly collection of short-form anime projects from Konami adapting lore vignettes featured in the card game, seperated into different arcs. While the Seeker of Sinful Spoils collection of shorts will be concluding release in December 2026, there are already plans for 2027, which will mark the release of Evil★Twin .

Are you still loving Yu-Gi-Oh after 30 years? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: 'Akazukin, Tabi no Tochuu de Shitai to Deau.' Reveals Additional Cast, Staff, First Promo for Winter 2027
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Aito Aoyagi 's Akazukin, Tabi no Tochuu de Shitai to Deau. ( Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story ) novel revealed additional cast, staff, first key visual (pictured), and first promotional video on Monday. The anime is scheduled to premiere in January 2027 on Tokyo MX, BS-NTV, and Yomiuri TV.

Cast Jill: Takuya Satou ( Super no Ura de Yani Suu Futari ) Antonio: Atsushi Tamaru ( Nanatsu no Maken ga Shihai suru ) Rodrigo: Motoko Kumai ( Cardcaptor Sakura ) Paolo: Koutarou Nishiyama ( Tougen Anki ) Oyayubi-hime: Sakiko Uran ( Toriko ) Narrator: Ryouko Shiraishi ( Fumetsu no Anata e )

Staff Main Animator: Ryouta Tamura ( Oroka na Tenshi wa Akuma to Odoru ), Satoru Kiyomaru ( Dead Mount Death Play chief animation director), Shunsuke Masuda ( Babanbabanban Vampire chief animation director), Yasuhiro Iwabuchi ( Reincarnation no Kaben animation director) Prop Design: Jazzline Monteron ( Reincarnation no Kaben animation director) Karakuri Design: Yoshinori Iwanaga ( Hyouken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu creature design) Art: Totonyan Art Director: Izumi Hoki ( Mao ), Hiroshi Katou ( Kidou Senshi Gundam: GQuuuuuuX ) Art Design: Hiroshi Katou, Yuichi Asami ( Rock wa Lady no Tashinami deshite ) Color Design: Chie Yoshimura ( Shoujo☆Kageki Revue Starlight ) Assistant Color Designer: Yumi Toriyama ( Boku no Kokoro no Yabai Yatsu color setting) Special Effects: Tomomi Ishihara ( Arifureta Shokugyou de Sekai Saikyou ) Director of Photography: Rieko Koike ( Chanto Suenai Kyuuketsuki-chan ) Editor: Daisuke Hiraki ( Nige Jouzu no Wakagimi ) Sound Director: Itsurou Kawasaki ( Kumichou Musume to Sewagakari ) Music: Jun Ichikawa ( Danjo no Yuujou wa Seiritsu suru? (Iya, Shinai!!) ) Music Production: Pony Canyon

Itsurou Kawasaki is directing the anime as well as penning the script at BENTEN Film . Manami Minakata ( Babanbabanban Vampire sub-character design) and Yuuko Yahiro ( Aharen-san wa Hakarenai ) are designing the characters.

Aoyagi published the comedy mystery novel through Futabasha in August 2020. The fourth volume went on sale in July 2025.

Kanoka Tana drew a manga adaptation from January 2023 to May 2025. It was first serialized in Monthly Action magazine before being transferred to Web Action . The fourth and final volume was published by Futabasha in June 2025.

title: Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story Anime Reveals 1st Trailer, More Cast & Staff, January 2027 Debut
content:
The staff for the television anime of Aito Aoyagi 's Akazukin, Tabi no Tochū de Shitai to Deau ( Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story , or literally Little Red Riding Hood Encounters a Dead Body During Her Journey.) novel revealed on Monday the anime's first trailer, first key visual, additional cast and staff members, and January 2027 debut.

The newly announced cast members are (image above from top left to bottom right):

• Takuya Satō as Jill

• Atsushi Tamaru as Antonio

• Motoko Kumai as Rodrigo

• Kōtarō Nishiyama as Paulo

• Sakiko Uran as Oyayubi-hime (Thumbelina)

• Ryōko Shiraishi as Narrator

Additional staff members include:

• Main Animator: Ryōta Tamura, Satoru Kiyomaru, Shunsuke Masuda, Yasuhiro Iwabuchi

• Prop Design: Jazzline Monteron

• Trick Design: Yoshinori Iwanaga

• Art: TOTONYAN

• Art Setting: Hiroshi Katō, Yuichi Asami

• Color Design Support: Yumi Toriyama

• Visual Effects: Tomomi Ishihara

• Sound Director: Itsurō Kawasaki

• Music: Jun Ichikawa

• Music Production: Pony Canyon

The anime will debut in January 2027 on the Tokyo MX , BS NTV , and Yomiuri TV channels. Crunchyroll also confirmed that it will stream the anime worldwide excluding Asia.

The anime will have its world premiere at New York Comic Con on October 9.

On the outskirts of town lived a girl called “Red Riding Hood.” One day, she found herself forced to embark on a journey for a certain purpose. Strangely enough, however, she kept getting swept up in incident after incident along the way. Using her innate curiosity and clever mind, Red Riding Hood set about solving each mystery. "Why is your criminal plan so sloppy?" This is the world of a fairy tale everyone knows—.

The anime will star Yume Miyamoto as Red Riding Hood, and Akira Sekine as Pinocchio.

Itsurō Kawasaki ( Baban Baban Ban Vampire , Cardfight!! Vanguard , Lady Jewelpet ) is directing the anime at Benten Film , and is also writing the script. Manami Minakata ( Baban Baban Ban Vampire sub-character designer, Grendizer U episode animation director) and Yūko Yahiro ( Aharen-san wa Hakarenai , Kaguya-sama: Love is War Season 2 ) are designing the characters. Izumi Hoki ( Detective Conan: Zero's Tea Time , MAO ) and Hiroshi Katō (2003 Astro Boy , Barakamon ) are the art directors, Tomoe Yoshimura ( The Heike Story , Mobile Suit Gundam Thunderbolt ) is in charge of color setting, Rieko Koike ( Baban Baban Ban Vampire , Diabolik Lovers ) is the compositing director of photography, and Daisuke Hiraki ( Backflip!! , Bocchi the Rock! ) is the editor.

Futabasha published Aoyagi's novel in August 2020.

Tanakanoka launched the novel's manga adaptation in Futabasha 's Monthly Action magazine in January 2023, where it serialized until the magazine ceased publication in February 2024. The manga then moved to Futabasha 's Web Action manga website in April 2024. The manga ended with its fourth compiled book volume, which shipped in June 2025.

The novel also inspired a live-action movie adaptation that streamed worldwide on Netflix in 2023. Kanna Hashimoto starred in the movie as Little Red Riding Hood.
author: ANN

Izumi Hoki ( Detective Conan: Zero's Tea Time , MAO ) and Hiroshi Katō (2003 Astro Boy , Barakamon ) are the art directors, Tomoe Yoshimura ( The Heike Story , Mobile Suit Gundam Thunderbolt ) is in charge of color setting, Rieko Koike ( Baban Baban Ban Vampire , Diabolik Lovers ) is the compositing director of photography, and Daisuke Hiraki ( Backflip!! , Bocchi the Rock! ) is the editor.
Futabasha published Aoyagi's novel in August 2020.

Tanakanoka launched the novel's manga adaptation in Futabasha 's Monthly Action magazine in January 2023, where it serialized until the magazine ceased publication in February 2024. The manga then moved to Futabasha 's Web Action manga website in April 2024. The manga ended with its fourth compiled book volume, which shipped in June 2025.
The novel also inspired a live-action movie adaptation that streamed worldwide on Netflix in 2023. Kanna Hashimoto starred in the movie as Little Red Riding Hood.

title: The Record of a Fallen Vampire Manga Gets TV Anime in 2027
content:
A website opened on Monday to announce the television anime adaptation of Kyo Shirodaira and Yuri Kimura 's The Record of a Fallen Vampire ( Vampire Jūjikai ) manga, which will debut in 2027. The website also revealed the anime's teaser promotional video, teaser visual, and main cast and staff members.

The anime will star:

Yūma Uchida as Rose Red Strauss, a pure-blooded vampire and the last king of the Night Kingdom

Aino Shimada as Bridget Irving Frostheart, a Dhampir who has lived for over 1,000 years

Mankyū ( Fist of the North Star: Strawberry Flavor , Migi & Dali , The Ramparts of Ice two seasons) is directing the anime at Zero-G and Liber , and is also in charge of series scripts. jimao ( Mechanical Marie , The Ice Guy and His Cool Female Colleague prop designer) is designing the characters, and Evan Call ( Frieren: Beyond Journey's End two seasons, Violet Evergarden ) is composing the music.

Viz Media published the manga in English physically. Yen Press and Square Enix 's Manga UP! Global service publishes the manga digitally. Viz Media describes the story:

A tale of the Vampire King's tragic love and its consequences Thousands of years ago, Vampire King Akabara "Red Rose" Strauss lost both his kingdom and his queen. Since humans were unable to kill the queen, they sealed her away, erecting thousands of fake seals so that the king would never find her true location. Despite being pursued by relentless dhampires, Akabara continues to search for his queen to this day… Akabara's quest takes a sinister turn when an entity called the Black Swan appears. The Black Swan inhabits the body of a young human girl every 50 years, giving her the power to destroy the Vampire King and his queen. With each incarnation the Black Swan grows stronger--will the 49th Black Swan mean the end of Akabara?

Shirodaira and Kimura launched the manga in Square Enix 's Shonen Gangan magazine in December 2003. The company shipped the ninth and final compiled book volume in April 2007. Viz Media published the manga in English in May 2008, and it shipped the ninth volume in May 2010.

Shirodaira and Kimura will launch a new manga in the series titled Vampire Jūjikai : Inu ni wa Inu no Uta (The Record of a Fallen Vampire: A Dog's Song for Dogs) in Shonen Gangan on October 9.

title: Manga 'Vampire Juujikai' Gets TV Anime For 2027
content:
Production company Pony Canyon opened an official website for the television anime adaptation of Kyou Shirodaira 's Vampire Juujikai ( The Record of a Fallen Vampire ) on Monday revealing the main cast pair, staff, a teaser visual (pictured), and a teaser promo. The anime is scheduled to premiere in 2027.

Voice actors Yuuma Uchida ( Jujutsu Kaisen ) and Aino Shimada ( Kakkou no Iinazuke ) will be joining the cast as Akabara Strauss and Bridget Irving Frostheart, respectively.

Staff Director, Series Composition: MANQ ( Koori no Jouheki ) Character Design: jimao Music: Evan Call ( Sousou no Frieren ) Animation Production: Zero-G , Liber

Kyou Shirodaira penned the dark fantasy manga in Square Enix's Monthly Shounen Gangan magazine from august 2003 to february 2007 with Yuri Kimura doing the illustrations. Square Enix published the manga in nine volumes from December 2003 to April 2007.

Viz Media licensed the manga in English under the title The Record of a Fallen Vampire and released all nine volumes between May 2008 and May 2010.

Synopsis There is a legend that tells of how the world was almost destroyed thousands of years ago by the vampire queen after she unleashed her latent powers. Despite their efforts, the humans were unable to defeat her, and thus resorted to sealing her away until the time came that they would be powerful enough to destroy the seal and kill her. However, the humans are not the only ones after the seal. Having cast aside his kingdom and betraying his own race and the dhampirs (half-vampires), the vampire king is persistently searching, even to this day, for where his queen has been sealed away so he may break the seal and free her before the humans do. Fearing that once the king and queen are reunited, they shall continue to destroy the world together, the humans and dhampirs hunt the king, using any method possible. (Source: Anime Source)

title: Psikyo Memories Collection Reveals Full List of Games, February 18 Release
content:
Edia opened the official website for its Psikyo Memories , a collection of '90s arcade scrolling shooter games by Psikyo, on Monday. The company also revealed the full list of games included in the collection, and its February 18, 2027 release for Nintendo Switch 2 and PlayStation 5. The game's pre-order also opened on Monday.

The collection will include the following games:

• Strikers 1945

• Strikers 1945 II

• Strikers 1999

• Gunbird

• Gunbird 2

• Gunbarich

• Zero Gunner 2

• Sol Divide: Sword of Darkness

• Dragon Blaze

• Samurai Aces Episode I

• Samurai Aces Episode II: Tengai

• Samurai Aces Episode III: Sengoku Cannon

The game collection will also feature a gallery of archive materials from the games.

Psikyo's arcade shooters have had previous collection releases on the PlayStation 2, PlayStation 4, and Switch. The latest release is Psikyo Shooting Stars Alpha and Psikyo Shooting Stars Bravo , which launched on the Switch in 2020, and on the PS4 in 2022.

Psikyo announced a Psikyo Shooting Collection release for the PlayStation 5 in 2020, but has since not released it. The collection would have included the same 12 works listed above.

title: Macross 7, Synduality: Noir Animator Kenichirō Katsura Dies at 59
content:
Animator Satoko Miyachi announced on her X (formerly Twitter ) account on Monday that her husband, animator Kenichirō Katsura , died on September 30, while undergoing medical treatment for an illness. He was 59.

A private funeral was held with only close relatives in attendance.

Miyachi expressed her deepest thanks to all the fans who loved Katsura's works, the animation studios, and all the staff he worked with throughout his life.

Katsura most recently worked as animation director for Gintama: The Movie 2026: Yoshiwara in Flames (image right), and as key animator for That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime the Movie: Tears of the Azure Sea . The films opened in Japan on February 13 and February 27, respectively.

Katsura was chief animation director for the two seasons of Synduality: Noir , The Fruit of Grisaia , the second season of Shy (5 episodes), The Eden of Grisaia (10 episodes), How to keep a mummy (9 episodes), and That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime (8 episodes), among others.

He also directed the Utawarerumono OAV and the Hi・Me・Go・To OAV.

He was also an episode key animator for anime series such as BLUE LOCK 2nd Season , Date A Live II , Encouragement of Climb seasons 2 & 3, the 1995 Magic Knight Rayearth 2 , Noir , Oishinbo , and the 1989 Ranma ½ series, among others. He was also the key animator for the first part of the Mobile Suit SD Gundam Festival film, and for the OVA episodes of Mobile Suit SD Gundam Mk V and Mobile Suit SD Gundam: SD Gundam Legend .

Katsura also worked as animation director for Macross 7 (4 episodes), as episode director and animation director for the third episode of the Macross 7 Encore OAV , as character designer for Macross 7 Plus , and as character designer and animation character designer for Macross 7 the Movie: The Galaxy's Calling Me! .

The official X/ Twitter account for the Knight's & Magic anime posted its own condolences on Monday. Katsura was the anime's character designer and chief animation director.

title: Manga 'Hirayasumi' Ends in Two Chapters
content:
The official X (formerly Twitter) account for author Keigo Shinzou announced on Monday that the Hirayasumi manga will end in two more chapters.

Shinzou began drawing the manga in Big Comic Spirits in April 2021. Shogakukan published the tenth volume on April 30.

VIZ Media licensed the manga in English in October 2023, with the latest ninth volume released on May 19.

Hirayasumi was nominated for the 15th and 17th Manga Taisho . The manga also placed among the top 20 titles in the male readers category in the 2023 Kono Manga ga Sugoi! rankings and MyAnimeList's 2024 edition of You Should Read This Manga . The series won the 71st Shogakukan Manga Award in 2026.

A television anime adaptation produced by Production +h. is scheduled to premiere in January 2027.

Synopsis Living in Asagaya, 29-year-old Hiroto Ikuta spends his days working at his part-time job and chatting with the locals. He likes visiting Hanae Wada most, a grumpy yet kind elderly woman whom Hiroto calls "Granny." Hiroto's time with Granny is sadly cut short when she passes away from a heart attack. To his surprise, Hiroto inherits Granny's house as she never married or had children.

Three months later, 18-year-old Natsumi Kobayashi moves from her hometown to attend art school. With nowhere else to go, she stays with her cousin Hiroto, whom she has not seen in years. Despite their opposing personalities, the pair begin living under the same roof as they struggle through their seemingly mundane lives. [Written by MAL Rewrite]

Manga special site: https://bigcomicbros.net/work/48647/ Manga official X (formerly Twitter): @ hirayasumi0426
